facts.text: Hotel Sacher Vienna opened in 1876.
facts.excerpt: Since its opening in 1876, Hotel Sacher Vienna has been an integral part of Vienna’s cultural and social life.

facts.text: The hotel was founded by Eduard Sacher, son of the creator of the Original Sacher-Torte, and under Anna Sacher became a meeting place for nobility, artists and businessmen.
facts.excerpt: Founded in 1876 by Eduard Sacher, the son of the creator of the Original Sacher-Torte, Hotel Sacher soon became the top address for Viennese high society. Under the renowned Anna Sacher, it evolved into a meeting place for nobility

facts.text: Franz Sacher created the Original Sacher-Torte in 1832, and it is still handcrafted in 34 steps.
facts.excerpt: The foundations of Sacher date back to 1832, when Franz Sacher created the Original Sacher-Torte. To this day, it is handcrafted in 34 steps

facts.text: Since 1934 the hotel has been managed by the Gurtler family and is privately owned.
facts.excerpt: Since 1934, the hotel has been carefully managed by the Gürtler family – privately owned and committed to tradition, excellence and authenticity.

facts.text: Hotel Sacher Vienna is a privately owned, family-run five-star superior hotel and a member of The Leading Hotels of the World.
facts.excerpt: Today, Hotel Sacher Vienna is one of the few privately owned, family-run five-star superior hotels and a member of _The Leading Hotels of the World_.

facts.text: The rooms and suites were designed by co-owner Alexandra Winkler with French designer Pierre-Yves Rochon.
facts.excerpt: The rooms and suites were designed by co-owner Alexandra Winkler in collaboration with internationally renowned French star designer Pierre-Yves Rochon.

facts.text: Rooms feature marble bathrooms.
facts.excerpt: Selected materials, marble bathrooms and elegant interiors combine classic Viennese character with modern comfort

facts.text: Some rooms look onto Karntner Strasse, the Vienna State Opera or the Albertina Museum; others overlook the quiet Maysedergasse or the courtyard.
facts.excerpt: Some of the Hotel Sacher Vienna rooms have views of the iconic Kärntner Straße, Vienna State Opera or the Albertina Museum. Others overlook the quiet Maysedergasse or the courtyard.

facts.text: Each room has a complimentary minibar with non-alcoholic beverages.
facts.excerpt: A complimentary minibar with non-alcoholic beverages

facts.text: The Opera Penthouse Suite has a spacious terrace and views over Vienna.
facts.excerpt: Opera Penthouse Suite – with spacious terrace and views over Vienna

facts.text: The hotel is steps from the Vienna State Opera, the Albertina Museum and St. Stephen's Cathedral, with the main sights reachable on foot.
facts.excerpt: just steps away from the world-famous Vienna State Opera, the Albertina Museum and the magnificent St. Stephen’s Cathedral. The finest sights of Vienna are easily accessible on foot.

facts.text: The hotel is within steps of Karlsplatz/Oper, a hub for U-Bahn lines U1 and U4.
facts.excerpt: Guests are within steps of **Karlsplatz/Oper**, a major hub for **U-Bahn (subway) lines U1 and U4**.

facts.text: Restaurant Rote Bar serves authentic Austrian cuisine with classic Viennese dishes made with seasonal and regional ingredients.
facts.excerpt: Rote Bar: Our head chef serves authentic Austrian cuisine at the highest level, featuring classic Viennese dishes made with seasonal and regional ingredients.

facts.text: Restaurant Grune Bar offers international haute cuisine with modern accents and regional influence, with set menus and a la carte.
facts.excerpt: Grüne Bar: Offers a special experience of international haute cuisine with modern accents and regional influence. Both set menus and à la carte options are available.

facts.text: Cafe Sacher Wien serves Original Sacher-Torte alongside Viennese coffees, apple and curd cheese strudel.
facts.excerpt: Alongside our coffees, we serve the Original Sacher-Torte, traditional Viennese apple and curd cheese strudel, as well as selected creations from the Sacher Patisserie.

facts.text: At lunch and dinner Cafe Sacher Wien serves classic Viennese dishes such as Wiener Schnitzel, veal goulash and Original Sacher Sausages, plus vegetarian and vegan options.
facts.excerpt: Enjoy favourites such as Wiener Schnitzel, creamy veal goulash and Original Sacher Sausages, alongside lighter dishes and a selection of vegetarian and vegan options.

facts.text: The Original Sacher-Torte is sold in various sizes at the in-house Sacher Shop, with worldwide shipping for online orders.
facts.excerpt: Yes, the Original Sacher-Torte is available in various sizes at our in-house Sacher Shop. You will also find fine souvenirs and exclusive products there. Online orders with worldwide shipping are also available

facts.text: The Sacher Boutique Spa has a hammam, sauna and fitness room.
facts.excerpt: Guests can also enjoy soothing moments in the hammam, sauna or modern fitness room.

facts.text: Spa massages use premium oils from Ligne St. Barth.
facts.excerpt: Deeply relaxing massages with premium oils from Ligne St. Barth

facts.text: The hotel has no swimming pool.
facts.excerpt: Unfortunately, we don’t have a swimming pool on site.

facts.text: The concierge service is available around the clock.
facts.excerpt: Yes, our experienced concierge service is available around the clock

facts.text: On request the hotel organizes horse-drawn carriage rides through the Old Town, Danube river cruises and customized city tours.
facts.excerpt:
Horse-drawn carriage rides through the Old Town
- Danube river cruises
- Customized city tours

facts.text: Private tours of the historic hotel can be arranged on request.
facts.excerpt: Yes, we are happy to organize exclusive private tours of our property upon request

facts.text: The Petit Sacher offer includes selected children's dishes in all the restaurants, and children have complimentary access to the breakfast buffet.
facts.excerpt: Yes, our “Petit Sacher” offer includes selected children’s dishes available in all our restaurants. Additionally, children have complimentary access to the breakfast buffet.

facts.text: Breakfast is generally not included in the room rate.
facts.excerpt: Breakfast at Hotel Sacher Vienna is generally not included in the room rate

facts.text: There is no formal dress code, but smart casual to elegant attire is recommended in Rote Bar and Grune Bar.
facts.excerpt: There is no formal dress code. However, we kindly ask guests to dress in a manner appropriate to the elegant atmosphere of our hotel. In our restaurants such as the Rote Bar and Grüne Bar, we recommend smart casual to elegant attire.

facts.text: Hotel Sacher Vienna ranked No. 42 in The 50 Best Hotels 2026, its second consecutive year on the list.
facts.excerpt: Hotel Sacher Vienna has once again been named among The 50 Best Hotels, ranking No. 42 worldwide in 2026. For the second consecutive year, we are part of this international ranking

facts.text: For the 150th anniversary, two Erwin Wurm sculptures stand at the hotel entrance until November 2026.
facts.excerpt: To mark the beginning of the anniversary year in March 2026, Hotel Sacher Vienna presents two sculptures by internationally renowned Austrian artist Erwin Wurm at the hotel entrance

facts.text: Hotel Sacher was once the rendezvous for high society including Gustav Klimt (brand-wide page).
facts.excerpt: Once the rendezvous for high society, including the renowned artist Gustav Klimt, Hotel Sacher has remained a cultural cornerstone
